datasets: 311 Customer Service Requests 2026 (ArcGIS FeatureServer, paged GeoJSON, fetched at runtime: 706,938 records)
Vacant Building Rehabs (Open Baltimore GeoJSON download, fetched at runtime: 12,647 records)
concurrency_primitives: one fetcher goroutine per source with sync.WaitGroup (pipeline.go:38-47); bounded jobs/parsed channels (workers*8) feeding N parser goroutines, WaitGroup closes parsed (pipeline.go:34-61); single collector goroutine aggregates (pipeline.go:62-65); context.WithTimeout + select on ctx.Done() for every send (pipeline.go:110-114,152-156,213-217)
design_patterns: Producer/worker/collector Pipeline; Source configuration object selecting live / -offline / -from-raw providers; no Strategy/Factory/Builder interfaces
questions: Which neighborhoods have the strongest combined signal of 2026 311 request volume and vacant-building rehab locations?
Where are the largest concentrations of vacant-building rehab locations?
Which neighborhoods have the most 311 requests whose recorded status is not closed/complete/resolved/cancelled?
Which 311 service request types are relatively more common in high-rehab neighborhoods?
Do neighborhoods rank similarly by 311 request volume and vacant-building rehab locations? (Spearman)
stakeholders: Department of Housing and Community Development
overview: Four-file single-package Go CLI whose default mode pages the live ArcGIS 311 FeatureServer (2,000 records/page) and downloads the Vacant Building Rehabs GeoJSON concurrently, saves raw pages to data/raw, parses features in a bounded worker pool, reduces them to per-neighborhood counters in one collector, and writes Markdown/CSV/JSON reports plus a terminal dashboard. Streaming design is excellent (53 MB RSS for 707k records) and race-clean, but there are no tests, no interfaces, a dead identity function, and dense one-line formatting.
stakeholder_value: Q4 is a real cross-dataset finding DHCD could use: SW-Boarding (3.8x), SW-Cleaning (3.7x), HCD-Vacant Building (2.7x) and Dirty Alley (2.5x) requests are enriched in the top-quartile rehab neighborhoods (Broadway East, McElderry Park, Oliver, Belair-Edison), and Spearman 0.77 shows rehab permits and 311 load co-locate. Q2 and Q3 are single-dataset top-5 lists, Q5 restates the summary statistic, and the 'requests per 100 rehab locations' column is meaningless where rehabs are rare (Downtown 41,781.8); nothing is normalised per capita.
issues: No tests (go test: no test files).
Concurrency limited to fetch and parse; aggregation and analysis are sequential in one collector.
Q2 and Q3 are single-dataset; Q5 duplicates the executive summary; 'requests per 100 rehab locations' ratio is not meaningful.
Default live run took 6m47s and downloaded ~600 MB of raw pages; README does not warn about duration or size; bundled excerpts (250 features each) are too small to analyse.
Dead code (cleanNeighborhood identity), stats and file I/O mixed in analysis.go, dense formatting.
run-macos.sh not executable in archive (README does instruct chmod +x).
Bundled reports/ are stale outputs from the student's 2026-10-11 run and are overwritten on each run.
rationale: Full marks for build, memory, runs and README: the live default run fetched and processed the complete real datasets within the time limit with a genuinely streaming, race-clean pipeline. Real_data is capped at 10 by the rubric because the full data is fetched rather than bundled; concurrency is 10 because only fetch/parse is parallel; architecture 9 for a clear but single-package, untested, pattern-light codebase; stakeholder 9 because two questions are single-dataset and one metric is meaningless. Total 78 (C).
